first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the inherited evidence suggests that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction can improve these leading indicators. I would verify both records before committing, then run a guarded test that measures qualified revenue and downstream retention—not just completion or activation—to avoid sacrificing lead quality.

mid.rationale: Run a guarded SMB-focused test of the shortened onboarding flow, prioritizing recovery of the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline while measuring qualified revenue, 30-day retention, and segment quality. The verified onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and retention, making it the strongest fit for sustainable revenue. Signup simplification also improved SMB activation and qualified revenue but reduced retention, so it should not be the primary intervention this cycle.

final2.rationale: The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled price-sensitive SMB churn make targeted promotional pricing the most urgent response. Run a tightly scoped SMB offer with eligibility and duration limits, measuring qualified revenue, gross margin, retention, and expansion—not just acquisition—to control the risk of subsidizing low-value or already-converting accounts. This relies on the prior promotional-pricing result without additional source verification, so keep the rollout guarded.
